messages:
alex: heads-up — after the NVLink firmware roll last night we see KV cache memory climb on long-context workloads. paging rate spikes and a few PT sync warnings in logs. anyone else?

maria: saw that on the 3pm replay. longctx tests with batch_size=16 go from ~12GB -> 22GB over 5k steps. paging IOPS jump around 30s mark.

chris: can you paste the tail of the container log? curious if it's the async-evict path thrashing.

alex: yup — grabbing snippets.

alex: ```
[2026-02-14T15:23:11Z] kvcache: evict: iter=1 pages=64 latency=4.2ms
[2026-02-14T15:23:11Z] pagetable: sync_wait: unaligned-owner detected gpu=rtx6000 peer=h100
[2026-02-14T15:23:12Z] kvcache: pagewalk: fault->migrate retry=3
[2026-02-14T15:23:12Z] perf: kvcache_kb=12288 -> 22528 (5k tokens processed)
```

maria: that "unaligned-owner" line is the one. we've seen similar messages before but usually on nvlink topology changes. seems like the PT shadow map isn't getting coherent after remap.

olivia: repro steps? I can run a focused job on mixed-gpu node. which commit?

alex: master@c2f9e7 with the dynamic-kernel-selection change + batching tweak (auto-window 2048 -> 4096).

chris: profiling snapshot from perf-bot on that run (flamegraph top): continuous evict + pagewalk consumes ~18% CPU on host and stalls kernels waiting for PT sync. batching ups window -> larger KV working set -> more cross-gpu PT churn.

perf-bot: ```
flame top: kvcache_eviction 18% | pagewalk_coalescer 9% | l2_migration 6% | inference_kernels 45%
trace: lots of repeated pagewalks for same logical key range
```

maria: interesting — kernel selection change prioritizes larger multi-query kernels when window >= 4096. those kernels do more concurrent KV writes, so pagetable metadata gets updated more aggressively and our shadow sync path hits a race.

olivia: can we mitigate by throttling concurrent PT writers? quick test: set kvcache.max_concurrent_pt_writers=2 and revert auto-window to 2048 to see if growth stops.

alex: started a canary with those flags on the mixed node. logs incoming.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/kvcache-throttle @ cluster-prod-3 (task id 78f4).

alex: early numbers look promising — memory stabilizing around 13GB, paging spikes reduced. but we still see occasional "pt_shadow_mismatch" warnings at low rate.

chris: I ran a local instrumented build and found the race: when two eviction workers try to remap adjacent segments, our PT writeback sets owner bits then returns before NVLink TLB invalidation completes on peer. peer then reads stale owner and issues a pagewalk -> migration -> reinjection, creating ghost allocations.

maria: so the fix needs an extra barrier after owner flip before acknowledging remap. cheap on slow paths, but must be optimized for H100's TLB flush cost.

olivia: propose short/medium plan: 1) keep throttle + revert auto-window (canary) 2) add PT owner barrier in runtime and add a microbenchmark to measure NVLink flush cost per arch 3) longer: add per-segment remap token and coalesced TLB invalidation path.

alex: +1. also adding unit test that fuzzes concurrent remap + evict on mixed GPUs. I'll file a bug and assign.

alex: bug: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-2026 (KV-PT-SYNC) — summary + logs attached.

chris: for the code patch, prefer a conditional barrier: only on cross-gpu remaps or when peer_arch != local_arch. avoids hurting same-gpu fast path.

maria: agreed. I'll prototype the barrier using existing async_fence API and run across h100/rtx/mi250 permutations.

perf-bot: scheduled perf runs for permutations: [h100+h100,h100+rtx6000,h100+mi250x,rtx6000+mi250x] — ETA 3h.

olivia: thanks — if canary holds we roll throttle as short-term patch and schedule the PT barrier for the next runtime patch.

alex: closing loop: canary ran 6h, no mem drift, paging IOPS down 3.5x. pushing rollback of auto-window now and flag for throttle default to 2 until patch lands.

maria: great. leaving notes in the kvcache docs about the knob and the expected perf implication.

alex: awesome work team :thumbsup:
